content.title: Timothée Chalamet Remains Silent on His Opera and Ballet Controversy as He Promotes 'Marty Supreme' in China Ahead of Oscars
content.text: NEED TO KNOW Timothée Chalamet has been promoting Marty Supreme in Asia as controversy swirls regarding his Feb. 24 comment regarding the popularity of ballet and operaThe actor has not yet addressed the situation publicly, even as an increasing number of performing artists and Hollywood figures take issue with him suggesting that "no one cares about" those two art formsChalamet is nominated for Best Actor at the 2026 Oscars on Sunday, March 15 Everybody seems to have an opinion on Timothée Chalamet's brief comments regarding the popularity of ballet and opera, except for the Marty Supreme star himself. A growing number of performing artists and figures in Hollywood have publicly chastised Chalamet, 30, in recent days for suggesting that "no one cares about" art forms like ballet and opera during his Variety and CNN town hall with Matthew McConaughey on Feb. 24. Chalamet, however, has yet to address the situation, even while promoting his film abroad. On Friday, March 6, the Dune actor shared a number of photos to Instagram from Japan as he and Marty Supreme director Josh Safdie continue promoting the movie overseas. The pair also appeared in Beijing on Tuesday, March 10 for the movie's China premiere, where Chalamet appeared to be given a tapestry that reads: "To Timothée Chalamet: The absolute Supreme Marty. You are the Cinematic Chameleon / You are the Reigning God of Acting / You are the King of the Silver Screen / You are Our Sweet Tea," from fans of his in China. Timothée Chalamet in Beijing on March 10, 2026. ADEK BERRY / AFP via Getty Chalamet made his comment on ballet and opera as he discussed Hollywood's efforts to "keep movie theaters alive" and keep American audiences interested in going out to see new films with his Interstellar costar McConaughey, 56, on Feb. 24. "I don't want to be working in ballet, or opera, or things where it's like, 'Hey, keep this thing alive, even though like no one cares about this anymore.' All respect to all the ballet and opera people out there," he said during the talk. The actor appeared to recognize that his comments could be seen as disparaging and immediately added, "I just lost 14 cents in viewership, I just took shots for no reason." Some of Chalamet's critics, such as Grammy Award-winning opera singer Isabelle Leonard, responded in comments on an Instagram video of the moment in question shared by Variety and wrote that she felt "shocked that someone so seemingly successful can be so ineloquent and narrow minded in his views about art while considering himself as artist as I would only imagine one would as an actor." Timothée Chalamet on March 10, 2026. VCG/VCG via Getty Rapper Doja Cat initially also criticized Chalamet's comments in a TikTok video she has since deleted. The following day, she backtracked on her own criticism of Chalamet and admitted in a second TikTok video, "I know nothing about opera. I know nothing about ballet." “What I was doing yesterday was virtue signaling because I wanted to connect and I knew that Timothée’s goof up was something that I could leverage in order for people to connect with me and f--- with me,” she said in her follow-up video. “And it’s easy. It’s a modern way to garner clicks, likes, approval and all kinds of things like that from people. And so I did that yesterday, and I didn’t really think about why I was doing it.” Related Stories The controversy continues to gain attention as the 98th Academy Awards approach on Sunday, March 15, where Marty Supreme is nominated for nine Oscars, including Best Picture and a Best Actor nod for Chalamet, which he shares with Sinners star Michael B. Jordan, as well as Leonardo DiCaprio (One Battle After Another), Wagner Moura (The Secret Agent) and Ethan Hawke (Blue Moon). Conan O'Brien is returning to host the Oscars live on Sunday, March 15, at 7 p.m. ET on ABC and streaming on Hulu.
